subject.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these plugin-path and SecretRef fallback conditions at the proposed critical/warning severities, including the resulting audit and Doctor lint failure behavior for existing operator configurations?
rationale: The implementation can detect the conditions safely, but code review cannot determine whether the proposed security-policy classification and compatibility impact match maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve proposed policy
options.body: Keep the critical plugin-path and warning SecretRef classifications, document the automation impact, and land after an exact-head rebase and checks.

options.title: Reduce compatibility impact
options.body: Keep the diagnostics but lower or otherwise adjust severities so existing audit and Doctor automation does not newly fail without explicit opt-in.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Land only the configured plugin-path audit and defer SecretRef fallback policy until a broader safe-inspection contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve proposed policy
recommendation.body: Keep the critical plugin-path and warning SecretRef classifications, document the automation impact, and land after an exact-head rebase and checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision primarily concerns SecretRef resolution boundaries and security-policy behavior adjacent to this person's recent work.
